# Agency request package

> Fictional sample for the Budget Atlas prototype. Not an official document.

BR-2028-0042 · draft v1

## Context

The agency identifies a flood-damaged bridge on a federal road and requests $10 million for a bridge-repair program. The request explains the need, proposed work, and estimated cost.

## Sample record

- **Budget year:** FY 2028
- **Program:** Flood-Damaged Bridge Repair
- **Requested:** $10,000,000
- **Priority site:** Cedar Creek Bridge · fictional

Restore a flood-damaged federal-road crossing used by school buses and emergency vehicles. Request condition-based repairs, design support, and access planning.

## Package contents

- Justification narrative — Word / PDF-style working document
- Estimate workbook — Spreadsheet / budget-table extract
- Leadership briefing — Presentation outline

## Structured request

The proposed line items are also available as 02-request-v1.json for PR review.

activities.verification_fit: Git and agency systems hold the working request and its revisions. Review discussion stays with the documents.

activities.name: OMB review and passback
activities.example: The agency opens a PR for the $10 million request. OMB’s review records the passback decision and line-item direction. The agency commits a revision or appeal; approval and merge settle the document for the next stage.
activities.example_document: PR review summary, revised request, and settlement record

artifact.title: Passback as a pull request review
artifact.format: A reimagined workflow: the review summary records the formal direction, comments explain individual changes, and commits carry the agency response. Merging approves the settled document version.
decisions: Retain the proposed $10 million program level.
Put routes serving essential access first.
Replace uniform allowances with condition-based estimates and show quarterly phasing.
artifact.body: Agency response v2: revised the bridge priority list and cost schedule; added quarterly phasing. This planning exchange does not enact an appropriation.

# Sample passback review summary

> Fictional walkthrough. No actual GitHub review, merge, or OMB decision is asserted.

## Agency request

BR-2028-0042: $10 million for the bridge-repair program.

## OMB review — changes requested

Retain the $10 million planning level. Prioritize essential-access routes and revise the estimating basis and quarterly delivery plan.

### Line-item comment: priority-bridge-repairs / justification

Replace uniform allowances with condition-based estimates. Explain how the priority list protects school-bus and emergency access.

## Agency response — revision v2

Revision v2 updates the justification and delivery milestones. The $10 million request is unchanged. This walkthrough accepts the direction; an appeal could instead be attached to the review.

## Settlement

The reviewer approves and merges the revised request document. This approves a planning document; it does not enact an appropriation.

## Optional independent verification

An approved-document digest may later be anchored when a shared independently verifiable history is useful. Draft comments and revision discussions remain in Git. No blockchain submission is required for this review.

# President’s budget — program excerpt

> Fictional sample for the Budget Atlas prototype. Not an official document.

PBR-2028 · illustrative excerpt

## Context

The President’s budget proposes $10 million for the bridge-repair program and is transmitted to Congress. The proposal does not itself provide spending authority.

## Sample record

- **Budget year:** FY 2028
- **Proposed program level:** $10,000,000
- **Purpose:** Repair flood-damaged federal-road bridges

The Administration proposes a bridge-repair program focused on restoring essential access. The request includes project prioritization and expected delivery milestones. Congress will consider funding through legislation.

activities.verification_fit: The published proposal can be referenced by version and digest. Publication and transmittal remain the source records.

# Allotment decision

> Fictional sample for the Budget Atlas prototype. Not an official document.

AL-001 · agency funds control

## Context

The agency allots $1 million of the apportioned $2.5 million to the district responsible for the bridge. The district’s allotment and its restrictions are recorded in the funds-control system.

## Sample record

- **Parent:** AP-001 · $2,500,000
- **District request:** $1,000,000

The approved $1 million allotment goes to the district responsible for Cedar Creek Bridge. The remaining $1.5 million is available for other allotments in this simplified scenario.

## Decision flow

AP-001: $2.5 million apportioned

Does the $1 million request fit the available amount, purpose, and approval conditions?

- Yes: Record AL-001: $1 million allotted
- No: Return for review; no allotment recorded

$1.5 million remains unallotted

activities.verification_fit: Agency funds control may be served by its own signed log. Share selected approved changes only when independent verification adds value.

## Context

After the necessary reviews, the district signs a $750,000 bridge-repair contract. The agency records this obligation against the $1 million allotment.

activities.verification_fit: Keep the contract and obligation in their systems. Selected approval evidence can link the obligation to its authorized allocation.

activities.name: Closeout and audit
activities.example: Later, after the remaining work and final $250,000 payment are complete, staff reconcile the contract and retain its audit trail. The appropriation account closes under its own availability and cancellation rules.

artifact.title: Closeout and reconciliation note
artifact.format: Project reconciliation and audit evidence are retained together. Appropriation-account closeout follows its own applicable rules.
artifact.body: After final acceptance and the remaining payment, staff reconcile the contract and retain the approval trail. Unused allotment and account balances are addressed under the applicable funds-control and account-closeout rules.

# Closeout and reconciliation note

> Fictional sample for the Budget Atlas prototype. Not an official document.

CO-001 · illustrative later-stage record

## Context

Later, after the remaining work and final $250,000 payment are complete, staff reconcile the contract and retain its audit trail. The appropriation account closes under its own availability and cancellation rules.

## Sample record

- **Contract total:** $750,000
- **First payment:** $500,000 · PAY-001
- **Later final payment:** $250,000 · outside the live snapshot
- **Reconciled total:** $750,000

After final acceptance and the remaining payment, staff reconcile the contract and retain the approval trail. Unused allotment and account balances are addressed under the applicable funds-control and account-closeout rules.

activities.verification_fit: A closeout digest or evidence manifest can help later reviewers check retained records and their amendment history.

timeframe: Follow one funding request through enactment, execution, and closeout. Appropriations have different availability periods, and their lifecycle can span multiple fiscal years.
